acceptance.assertion: Deterministic representative 1,000-entry and 10,000-entry catalog fixtures exercise the current CommonProject schema, public location modes, digital taxonomy, translations, relations, provenance and content-addressed details without weakening validation.

The visible Commonworld runtime starts from a bounded manifest and aggregate and loads only required compact shards and selected details; global search, map and digital navigation no longer require the complete build-bound catalog in memory or in the startup payload.

The no-JavaScript and bootstrap-failure recovery path remains complete through bounded paginated indexes and canonical per-project pages rather than embedding every project card in the landing document.

Search, filtering, country and nearby discovery, globe rendering and digital navigation pass explicit transfer, parse, DOM, interaction and memory budgets at 1,000 and 10,000 entries; server-side search, PostGIS or PMTiles are introduced only when the measurements require them.

Every demand-loaded shard remains within the declared compressed budget at both scale tiers, and the contract defines a deterministic compatible prefix-depth migration before any generated shard can exceed that budget.

German and English surfaces, deep links, browser history, offline and blocked-network behavior, integrity and schema failures, retry, stale-response isolation and rollback pass on supported desktop, mobile and iPad profiles under fourfold CPU throttling, with physical-device evidence identified separately.

runtime_catalogue_cutover_authorized remains false until exact-head review, complete diff, green required CI, realistic scale evidence, rollback artifact, deployed generation and public production readback all pass; the cutover is reversible without rewriting catalog history.

Commonworld remains a public read-only discovery surface; mutable ingestion, moderation, visibility and publication truth stay assigned to the Weltgewebe handoff and are not duplicated in the static client.

approval.note: Do not remove the full bootstrap, no-JavaScript catalogue or public project routes until every acceptance gate is proven on the same exact head. Prefer measured static partitioning before adding backend infrastructure.

goal: Prove Commonworld with realistic 1,000-entry and 10,000-entry catalogues, then cut the visible product over from the complete build-bound bootstrap to bounded manifest, aggregate, shard and detail delivery while preserving discovery, map, digital navigation, recovery, privacy and rollback semantics.

metadata.source: Operator request following live Commonworld scalability audit
does_not_establish: that the current 65-entry production surface is already cut over
a requirement to deploy a backend, PostGIS, PMTiles or a separate search service without measured need
permission to remove recovery or public machine-readable surfaces
automatic queue, claim, dispatch, merge or deployment authority

rollback.strategy: Restore the compact build-bound bootstrap and complete generated recovery catalogue, disable visible shard-native delivery, retain immutable generation artifacts for diagnosis, and verify the restored public surface before any subsequent cutover attempt.

title: Prove 1k and 10k catalog cutover
